notes.title: Dev Diary #22 - New Map: The Mountains & Desert Maps!
notes.content:
Hi all!

[h1]# Progress Report[/h1]

I've gotten a basic version of exploration scenes for both mountains and the desert built, which just leaves the tundra as the last remaining biome that needs one! There's definitely more work to be done across all of them to create points of interest, fishing zone, wildlife, and so on though! That can all be added naturally as different features are implemented more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/19badf740a4180467dfd1c10823afc780109d62d.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/9247eb68f73201662992a62f4e0abc6d801753c8.png[/img]

[h1]# Project Status Update[/h1]

There are currently [u]11 tasks[/u] open to be completed before I consider [b]Journey Express[/b] to have hit the [b]Alpha[/b] milestone! Granted, I would not be surprised if more are added here and there, but the game is finally getting to where I want it to be!

I have since moved on to Bluesky for all social media updates! Feel free to follow me there! :)
https://bsky.app/profile/starcatgames.ltd

Thanks for reading!

notes.title: Dev Diary #21 - New Map: The Grasslands River!
notes.content:
Hi all!

Since last time, I've figured out all of the steps (I hope) required to take the forest exploration scene, and use it as the starting point for all future maps! 

As a starting point, I would like to have at least one map for each of the major biomes: [b]forest[/b], [b]grassland[/b], [b]mountain[/b], [b]desert[/b], and [b]mountain[/b]. Eventually, there would ideally be several possible variations for each in the future!

Observe!

notes.title: Dev Diary #20 - Bug Fixes, Boons & Banes
notes.content:
Hi all!

It has been a minute since the last update, but I'm working on getting things moving faster again!

[list]
[*] FIX: There were a number of minor bugs that cascaded into a bigger overall problem with the in-game event resolution system. When a random event occurs, things should actually take effect when the player responds to it.
[*] FIX: A couple in-game events had mismatched event effects and conditions.
[*] CHANGE: Show each party member's last name in addition to their first name in the journal
[*] NEW FEATURE (WIP): I'm adding a new system for buffing or de-buffing the player's party overall for a given amount of time. The effects can for now either boost or reduce health and/or morale! For example, the [i]Clear Weather[/i] event slightly raises the party's health and morale for a short period of time.
[*] OTHER: I'm continuing to work on end game functionality like different UI screens and implementation
[/list]

I have since moved on to Bluesky for all social media updates! Feel free to follow me there! :)
https://bsky.app/profile/starcatgames.ltd


Thanks for reading!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #19 - A Bunch of Changes!
notes.content:
Hi all!

[list]
[*] COMPLETED: The fishing mini-game is now what I consider "complete"! I'll no doubt make some changes to it in the future, but it'll do the job for now. There are currently 3 obstacle layouts where you launch a ball in an attempt to land it in the catcher at the bottom, which randomly positions itself when you start. I'll add more variety in future updates!
[*] NEW FEATURE: I've added new achievements for traveling the various biomes across the world map!
[*] NEW FEATURE: Food consumption! While I still need to add and test values for different food items, party members should now eat food while traveling to stay healthy (and happy)!
[*] IN-PROGRESS: Work continues on the travel logic concerning health and treatment tracking. Being able to easily tell the state of your party members is important, and I need to polish that aspect up yet.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/2e1a1daeffd5441dac19376f117b8a7a7a6433ee.png[/img]
I post more updates (especially images/videos) over on Threads, feel free to check me out over there if you like!

[url=https://www.threads.net/@starcat.games.ltd/post/C-3_pcxIbSt?xmt=AQGzLr0e_nPmy8uePed7TF9DAeA8Gdgj0to9tAwjZoUuZQ style=button]Threads Link[/url]

Thanks for reading!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #18 - Fishing Mini-game Continued!
notes.content:
Hi all!

The fishing mini-game is now accessible in the exploration scene, so you can actually fish when looking at bodies of water!

Next up awarding fish based on how well you play, as well as making the plinko board more interactive and randomized!

See more here! [url=https://www.threads.net/@starcat.games.ltd/post/C-3_pcxIbSt?xmt=AQGzLr0e_nPmy8uePed7TF9DAeA8Gdgj0to9tAwjZoUuZQ style=button]Threads Link[/url]

notes.title: Dev Diary #17 - Fishing Minigame!
notes.content:
Hi all!

Well, it's been much longer since the last update than I would like, but I'm back with a new update!

I'm working on implementing the fishing minigame, which will be in the general style of Plinko! The idea being to catch the pinball down below while the obstacles do obstacle things, and try to get in your way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/2e1a1daeffd5441dac19376f117b8a7a7a6433ee.png[/img]

My goal is to have semi-randomized obstacle layouts as well as make them move around, while also letting the player pick where the catcher at the bottom is positioned in order to maximize the chance of catching the ball.

Thanks for reading!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #16 - Fishing
notes.content:
Hi all,

It's been far too long since the last update, but you know, life! ːsteamfacepalmː

Currently, there is work being done on a mini-game for fishing whilst exploring the wilderness. That will allow the player to catch (you guessed it!) fish for food, or perhaps even [REDACTED]!.

I'm working on the mechanics of the game now on the code side of things, while the artist that has done most of the UI so far is creating the new assets. I'm looking forward to sharing it all when it's done!

Until next time, thanks!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #15 - Travel Scene Progress
notes.content:
Hi all,

This update won't be particularly interesting visually, but there have been a bunch of changes under the hood to make things actually work as expected, particularly in the event system. 

Now when, for example, a party member breaks a leg or contracts a sickness, they will actually have that effect applied to their person. This will be tracked as the journey progresses, either worsening or improving depending on what the ailment is and if it has been treated properly.

Next on the list is further build-out of the events system and making sure that such things are working as expected over time in the game. 

Until next time, thanks!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #14 - 'New Game' Flow Complete!
notes.content:
Hi all,

[h3]New Game Flow / Main Menu Changes[/h3]

After fixing a boatload of bugs and wiring various things together, the new game flow is finally feature complete! This means a player can actually fully start a new game and get into the travel gameplay portion of [b]Journey Express[/b].

The next step is finishing the flow between [Travel Scene] <---> [Exploration Scene]. The main features that need to work are:

[list]
[*] Maintain consistent time of day from [Travel Scene] ---> [Exploration Scene].
[*] Finish testing weather & season features within [Exploration Scene]. 
[*] Track changes to inventory between [Travel Scene] <---> [Exploration Scene]. Need to be able to bring items back from exploring and add them to the travel inventory.
[/list]

Thanks!
- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #13 - New Assets & Campsite
notes.content:
Hi all,

This time around I have some new assets to show off, the first being a new character, The Peddler, who you may come across while traveling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/aec51e79b4ec6c0c56c3601156645c87eb7ffb13.png[/img]

Another one is the Campsite, where you'll be able to access your party's inventory and other information while you're out on the road.

notes.content:
Hi all,

Another short update this time around, but there's some fun stuff in the works.

[h3]Steps towards Alpha[/h3]

There's a fair bit to do yet, but my current focus is to wire everything that's currently implemented (or at least functional) together such that the game is playable from start to finish. 

Right now, you can proceed through the introductory dialogue, create a character, select a party contract to undertake, and set out to travel. Next step to finish implementing will be loading out the player's inventory with some kind of starter set of items, much like some of the Oregon Trail games did back in the day. After that, being able to reach your destination and be rewarded with cash and reputation is the last missing link.

Meanwhile, I need to work on patching up bugs and smoothing out rough edges.

I received the latest versions of assets for new portraits and some icons which are currently (as of today) added to builds of the game. Again, that brings the current number of portraits for player character customization and randomized party members from 2 up to 8.

I hope that by next time I write up a dev diary (#09), the game is much closer to if not already at a stage where I could call new builds "Alpha".

Thanks!

notes.title: Dev Diary #01 - Tile Inventory System, Bug Fixes & Steam Integration
notes.content:
Hi all!

This week was mostly bug-fixing & cleaning up things here and there. Up next I think I'll tackle some of the UI for viewing and managing party health, such as treatments for injuries and sicknesses.

I first wrote the tile-based inventory for the exploration side of the game over a year ago, and have been putting off fixing some long-standing bugs. Namely issues with rotating asymmetrical items like the rifle shown below (4x1). Luckily most of the issues I had were easy enough to fix once I dug into it.

The core concept is that you can bring items with you from your party's inventory when you go exploring. For example, you could bring a rifle and ammo along for hunting. On the other side of the coin is being able to bring things back with you when you're done. Collecting things like meat, plants, fish, and valuables will help keep your journey moving smoothly.

The limit to what you can carry will be determined by two things: your [b]weight capacity[/b], and what you can fit on your person via [b]the tiles[/b]. Certain tile zones will only allow certain types of items. Such as in the image below, the rifle will only be allowed to be carried in the backpack or shoulder tiles, and only small items can fit in the pockets.

A to-do item is to visually indicate where items can be dropped while dragging them so it's not just a guessing game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/627fcac2b64b58029f0a868db3070079169f6e61.gif[/img]

The other semi-major change is finally getting an implementation of hooking into Steam's API, mostly for [b]achievements[/b], but also just to get events and info from Steam.

That's all I've got this time around, thanks for reading!

- C

notes.title: Dev Diary #00 - Current State and Looking Forward
notes.content:
[h3]Hi all! I thought I’d take some notes here for information on the current state of Journey Express and where it will go from here.

While I’m happy with the progress made so far, there’s plenty of work to do! I’ll break it down by section of the game:[/h3]

[h2]Travel Gameplay[/h2]

About half of the game is intended to take place while traveling. That is, where you are actively managing your party or simply cruising along with your wagon in 2D.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/48bc6857366b224e71b4d615f2df1fd62ac8c0be.png[/img]

I consider a significant portion of the traveling gameplay loop feature-complete. For example: 
[list]
[*] navigating the map using the compass to control direction
[*] seamlessly moving between biomes
[*] dynamic time of day and weather
[*] managing the party inventory
[*] reading about discoveries & locations that have been found
[/list]
As far as things that are still in the to-do stage, some of the things on my immediate radar would be:
[list]
[*] finish testing health system
[*] finish UI for applying treatments on injuries or sicknesses
[/list]
[h2]Exploration Gameplay[/h2]

The other half of gameplay would be the exploration side of things, where you transition to 3D & a first-person perspective.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43607312/50e69f933f176a4203ed8253d0caa4101d907c77.png[/img]

This is where the majority of core development is yet to be done. That said, there are a number of fundamental pieces fairly well along:
[list]
[*] basic movement
[*] basic gun handling & hunting implementation
[*] basic wildlife AI
[*] time of day and weather control to match the party’s current travel state
[*] grid-based inventory management
[/list]
I anticipate the largest upcoming time-sink to be creating maps for the exploration gameplay to take place in. I experimented with procedural generation early on, but I disliked the general feel of them. By hand-making the maps I found that they seemed more organic, and generally more interesting. My current workflow, and by extension my goal, is to have some degree of randomness for each map as well as special occurrences that can only happen depending on time of day, weather, and more. The intention there being to keep each map interesting on subsequent visits.

That said, the trade-off is time to create them. Currently, there is a singular map (the one you would see in trailers and screenshots today) intended for use when traveling in forest biomes. 

---

[h2]Next steps[/h2]

My immediate next goal is linking together the current completed pieces of the game, with the end result being that Journey Express could move from pre-alpha to alpha. To me that would mean that the game is playable from clicking “New Game” all the way to being able to reach a destination and complete a journey.

The current missing pieces for that to happen would be:
[list]
[*] minor logic missing to connect the new game intro to the core travel loop
[*] adding a jumping off point for new journeys, mainly the ability to purchase initial supplies
[*] general bug fixes preventing consistent game flow
[*] finishing the river crossing event logic
[*] adding the journey completion UI flow
[/list]
It’s difficult to estimate timelines for getting given features done, more so when there are several on deck. Since this is a spare time project I do the best I can. 😅

—

For these dev-diaries, I’d really like to keep them coming regularly, perhaps every two weeks. 

Feel free to shoot any questions over to me on any of the socials, which I’ll link below.

That’s about all I have for now, I sincerely appreciate any and all interest & support for this project! Until next time.

Thanks!
Caden
